content.jointProblem: Can an uncertainty-aware spatial linkage workflow connect farm policies to defensible hail-exposure estimates and help identify potentially underpriced portfolio segments relative to municipality-level rating? The first experiment would audit a verified sample of policy-to-parcel matches and test whether the available daily five-kilometre weather data contain enough information for field-level differentiation before evaluating pricing relevance on held-out storms or years.

rationale.text: Đorđević has directly relevant experience harmonising cadastral schemas, coordinate systems and spatial data quality—the core integration work needed before policies can be linked reliably to weather layers.

sources.quote: Katarina Đorđević led the work package on data quality assessment and transformation infrastructure, supervising two research staff and one PhD student
with a focus on coordinate reference system alignment, attribute schema mediation, and topological quality assurance.

rationale.text: Her work provides methods for checking supplementary building-location data rather than treating OpenStreetMap as authoritative, which is relevant to resolving incomplete farm locations.

sources.quote: Results suggest OSM is useful for detecting unmapped structures but not for direct integration into formal cadastral registers without significant validation effort.
The framework is designed to be reusable and operationalised as a semi-automated QGIS model.

rationale.text: She has demonstrated Python-based checks for coordinate-reference metadata errors, supporting an automated quality-control stage for incoming spatial datasets.

sources.quote: The detection pipeline is implemented in Python using GDAL/OGR and produces a structured error report with suggested corrections.

rationale.text: Her PostGIS provenance work offers a basis for making policy-location transformations reproducible and inspectable.

sources.quote: A query interface allows users to retrieve full transformation chains for any geometry in the database.
The model is implemented as an extension to a PostGIS schema

constraints.text: Location matching must explicitly retain uncertainty and distinguish settlement-level addresses from verified insured buildings or fields; settlement centroids cannot be treated as field coordinates.

sources.quote: a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

constraints.text: Field-level hail inference must pass a resolution-feasibility check; assigning a weather-grid value to a parcel does not itself establish field-level hail intensity.

sources.quote: We do receive daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution
a storm can devastate one village and leave the farm two kilometres away untouched.

constraints.text: Validation must respect the limited historical sample and separate storms or years between development and testing rather than treating nearby claims from one storm as independent evidence.

sources.quote: We have three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies to work with.

constraints.text: The deliverable must include an operational handoff into the existing Python pricing workflow, with integration effort scoped to teams that also support day-to-day operations.

sources.quote: Python-based batch scoring pipeline for quarterly rating factor refresh
a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team who split their time between operational support and new product build.
which was completed but not yet integrated into the pricing system.

constraints.text: Start with a tightly scoped joint-project feasibility phase and confirm staffing and dates; the recorded availability limitation must not be assumed to have expired automatically.

sources.quote: limited availability for large new commitments before mid-2026; shorter consulting engagements or clearly scoped contract research are more feasible in the near term.

risks: The demonstrated cadastral, building-data and CRS methods have not been validated here for settlement-to-insured-field matching or hail reconstruction. The first experiment must test both linkage accuracy and weather-data sufficiency on independently verified locations.

Five-kilometre daily data may not resolve narrow hail tracks even after policy geocoding improves. Additional observations or a hail specialist may be necessary; their availability and cost are unknown.

The supplied material does not establish hail-specific modelling or insurance-pricing expertise. The researcher can anchor the spatial integration work, but actuarial and meteorological responsibilities need explicit ownership.
Three claim years may contain too few independent hail events for stable pricing conclusions. Availability of complete non-claim exposure, premiums, insured values and coverage terms is unknown.
Better exposure mapping may not explain the reported 18% excess claim cost; coverage mix, repair costs or other factors could contribute.

Current researcher availability, project budget, data-use permissions and company integration ownership remain unconfirmed. Limited operational capacity and a previous unintegrated mapping prototype create delivery risk.
questions: Can Đorđević confirm current availability, the scope she can lead, and whether a short feasibility phase within a joint project is workable?

Can the company supply insured parcel or building identifiers, address histories and a manually verified location sample? Do claim coordinates identify the damaged asset, the policyholder address or another location?

What variables does MeteoVoj actually provide, at what temporal aggregation, with what hail-validation evidence and licensing terms? Are radar, hail reports or other independent event observations accessible?

Can the first experiment compare verified-location linkage accuracy and weather discrimination within affected settlements, with predefined criteria for stopping field-level inference or seeking higher-resolution data?
Are policy-year exposure records available for both claimed and unclaimed policies, including premiums, insured values, deductibles, coverage type and event dates?
Who will own actuarial validation and hail interpretation, and what held-out comparison against municipality-level rating would justify further development?
What permissions and safeguards apply to policy, claims and cadastral data, and may external parcel or weather data be used in commercial pricing?
What budget, delivery window, IT owner and acceptance criteria are available for integrating and maintaining the workflow in the quarterly pricing pipeline?
